verdict.rationale: The IRS documents its own machine-to-machine filing rails: MeF, a system-to-system XML channel, and the IRIS Application to Application intake for information returns. These are the closest thing to bulk processing, but the evidence never states that many items can be handled in one operation. Both rails are gated behind e-file provider enrollment or a Transmitter Control Code, and the EIN assistant is explicitly limited to 1 EIN per responsible party per day. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of batch or multi-item submission, any bulk operations for account-level actions (payments, forms, EINs), ungated agent access, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: IRIS "receives information through two intake channels: IRIS Taxpayer Portal/UI and IRIS Application to Application (A2A)"
